audit_findings.title: Operating distributor interest may have been purged without adding the underlying notes
audit_findings.magnitude: $129.910 million of distributor notes, equal to $0.60 per diluted share and 4.1%-5.9% of stated scenario equity value; FY2025 interest income was $17.371 million, mostly from these notes
audit_findings.mechanism: Purging the distributor-note interest reduces OE while omitting the corresponding notes from the equity bridge, leaving neither the operating income nor the financed asset in value.
audit_findings.evidence: During Fiscal 2025, 2024, and 2023 the following amounts were recorded as interest income, the majority of which relates to these notes receivable (amounts in thousands):
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated classification mismatch, not merely a possibility. The filing identifies the distributor financing as part of the distribution system and says most interest income comes from it, while the valuation purges interest income and adds only cash. The omitted notes alone are large enough to move per-share value by about $0.60 before any collection or tax adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Rerun using one consistent treatment: retain after-tax IDP-note interest in OE as operating income, or exclude it and add the collectible fair value of the distributor notes to the bridge; do not count both.

audit_findings.title: The first forecast year may ignore a disclosed operating step-down
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the 53rd week contributed 1.7% of FY2025 sales, while the latest 28-week period showed sales down 1.2% and operating income down $30.604 million, or 17.1%, year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: An unnormalized 53-week anchor and immediate positive OE growth can overstate the first forecast cash flows and their subsequent compounding.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate our Fiscal 2026 sales will be lower than Fiscal 2025 due to the additional week in Fiscal 2025 and continued weakness in the fresh packaged bread category.
audit_findings.explanation: The lost week is demonstrated, and the anticipated operating weakness is corroborated by the latest results: the most recent quarter had sales down 4.0% and operating income down 27.1%. The OE effect cannot be isolated from the supplied record, but the decline is reasonably capable of erasing the valuation's downside-case margin of safety.
audit_findings.action: Normalize the anchor to 52 weeks, reconcile the first forecast year to the filed FY2026 results and sales outlook, and rerun all scenarios with an explicit first-year OE step before applying longer-term growth.

audit_findings.title: Near-term refinancing could raise the interest cost embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $400.0 million principal moves from a 3.5% coupon to a committed term facility priced at SOFR plus 0.875%-2.000%
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, the higher after-tax interest expense must reduce forecast OE rather than be handled through a debt deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The company will pay semiannual interest on the 2026 notes on each April 1 and October 1, beginning on April 1, 2017, and the 2026 notes will mature on October 1, 2026 .
audit_findings.explanation: The refinancing is no longer speculative: a $400 million delayed-draw term facility has been executed and is required to fund repayment of the October 1, 2026 notes. The exact future rate remains unresolved because it depends on SOFR, leverage and credit rating, but historical OE retains the expiring 3.5% cost and therefore does not represent the contracted financing structure.
audit_findings.action: Use the actual draw date, applicable pricing-grid margin and contemporaneous SOFR to calculate after-tax interest; replace the expiring-note interest in the first forecast year and rerun each scenario.

audit_findings.title: Known ERP spending is materially above the anchor-period run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $25 million-$30 million expected in FY2026, equal to 12.4%-14.9% of the $201.0 million OE anchor; approximately $275 million had been incurred by July 18, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: ERP cash spending can enter OE through operating expense, maintenance or implementation capex, cloud-computing assets, or prepaid service contracts; a mechanical growth forecast can omit the cash burden when classifications differ.
audit_findings.evidence: In Fiscal 2026, we expect costs for the upgrade of our ERP system (a portion of which may be expensed as incurred, capitalized, recognized as a cloud computing arrangement, or recognized as a prepaid service contract) to be approximately $30 million to $37 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing reduced the FY2026 estimate from $30 million-$37 million to $25 million-$30 million, but that amount remains material relative to anchor OE. The valuation provides no explicit staging or classification reconciliation, so omission is reasonably capable of overstating early cash flows and value.
audit_findings.action: Build a cash-based ERP schedule through the expected FY2027 completion, trace every dollar among expense, capex and other assets, subtract amounts not already captured in OE, and rerun without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Distributor-classification litigation could create unaccrued conversion and repurchase costs
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the latest filing reports 11 complaints, seven seeking class or collective treatment, and one $11.0 million settlement in principle already accrued
audit_findings.mechanism: Settlements and route repurchases reduce discrete OE or the equity bridge, while conversion to an employee model can permanently increase distribution labor, vehicle and related operating costs.
audit_findings.evidence: At this time, the company is defending ten complaints filed by IDPs alleging that they were misclassified as independent contractors.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure is real, but the record cannot estimate losses for the unresolved cases or establish that additional jurisdictions will require California-style conversion. The $11 million agreed settlement is already accrued; it does not quantify the remaining claims. California's prior $55 million settlement and $79 million of territory repurchases show possible scale but are not an estimate for the current cases.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $14.4 million of first-half FY2026 legal-settlement expense to anchor OE, obtain subsequent case and certification outcomes, and stress-test remaining settlements, route repurchases and recurring employee-model costs separately.

audit_findings.title: Simple Mills seller consideration may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.531 million outstanding, or $0.0716 per diluted share; 0.48%-0.71% of stated scenario equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The unpaid acquisition consideration is a liability that should be deducted directly from the equity bridge because its cost is not represented by recurring interest in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 21, 2025 , we completed the acquisition of 100 % of the equity interests of Purposeful Foods Holdings, Inc., the parent company of Simple Mills, Inc., for total consideration of approximately $ 848.6 million, which includes $ 17.9 million payable to the sellers upon realization of certain tax benefits acquired as part of the transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q demonstrates that $12.654 million remained current and $2.877 million remained long term, separately from reported debt. Its omission is therefore a demonstrated bridge error, but deducting it would reduce intrinsic value by only about $0.07 per share and the 30% buy-below threshold by about $0.05, versus the $3.00 gap between the $9.27 threshold and $6.27 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the unpaid $15.531 million in the next bridge rerun, subject to confirming any payment after July 18, 2026; no scenario-input change is otherwise required.
